exchanges.subject: October gross margin: mix vs rate
exchanges.body: Rachel, gross margin went from 27.998% in September to 27.818% in October, down 0.18 points, and it's mix, not pricing or cost. Mix: -0.24 points. Power units, our lowest-margin line (24.0% both months), rose from 36.0% to 38.6% of revenue (7,466,300 vs 6,800,000), while valves (about 33%) and service (38-39%) shrank. Rate: +0.06 points. Line margins were flat or slightly better: power units 24.0% both months, valves 32.9% vs 33.0%, pumps 25.1% both months, service 39.0% vs 38.0%. In October dollars, mix cost about 47,000 of margin and rate added about 12,000. exchanges.subject: October flux (vs September and budget)
exchanges.body: Rachel, October flux (after WD3 entries; threshold $10,000 or 10%). Revenue 19,331,480.25, +426,380.25 (+2.3%) vs Sept on units +2.3% (6,412 vs 6,268); +81,480.25 vs budget. Includes the 80,819.75 cutoff reversal; excludes Cascade. COGS +341,780 (+2.5%), gross margin 27.82% vs 28.00%: mix. Freight out 438,950, +36,650 (+9.1%) and +28,950 vs budget: more LTL shipments (61 vs 58) and fuel, plus Northfield accrued (27,300). Wages 1,708,900, +56,500 (+3.4%): 22 working days vs 21, overtime 4,120 vs 3,380 hours. Trade shows 31,640, +27,540: FabTech (budgeted 30,000), including the 2,500 deposit expensed from prepaids. Bank fees 3,475, +1,335 (+62%): September's 1,245 analysis charge posted 10/30 and the 90 merchant-fee correction; not recurring. IT and software 54,620, +5,720 (+11.7%): four laptops expensed under the capitalization threshold (4,720). Depreciation +1,280: September additions; the Hoosier fixture starts in November. Elena

threads.title: Call with Kevin Doyle, Brightline & Moss

exchanges.author: c_audit_assoc
exchanges.body: Hi Elena, it's Kevin. Two quick ones from the additions listing Marco uploaded. The Hoosier test fixture shows at forty-one thousand four hundred seventy-two dollars, but the invoice is thirty-eight thousand four hundred. What's the difference, and is it depreciating in October?

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: The difference is Ohio use tax. Hoosier is an Indiana vendor and charged no tax, so we self-assessed eight percent, three thousand seventy-two dollars, and capitalized it with the fixture, since our policy includes non-refundable taxes in cost. It went into service October twenty-seventh, so depreciation starts in November, at six hundred ninety-one dollars twenty a month.

exchanges.author: c_audit_assoc
exchanges.body: Great, that's clear. Last thing: could we get read-only access to NetSuite for the next two weeks? If it's easier, I could just use your login while we're on site.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: I can't share my login; everyone has to be on their own user for the audit trail. Read-only access is Rachel's call, and if she approves, Paul Brandt in IT will set up an auditor role for you. I'll ask her today.

exchanges.author: c_audit_assoc
exchanges.body: Perfect, thanks Elena.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Call note: Kevin Doyle (Brightline). (1) Hoosier fixture at 41,472.00 vs invoice 38,400.00: explained the 3,072.00 Ohio use tax (8.0%, Indiana vendor, none charged), capitalized under ACCT-410; in service 10/27, depreciation from November at 691.20 a month. (2) He asked for NetSuite read-only access, or to use my login: declined the login; access is Rachel's decision, Paul would set up an auditor role. Asking Rachel today.
